title_original: David Goldblatt and the Social Architecture of South Africa

blocks.text: Born in 1930 in Randfontein, South Africa, David Goldblatt lived and worked in Johannesburg until his death in June 2018. For nearly six decades, he photographed the people, landscapes and buildings of his country, using the camera as a tool of social criticism, and he came to be regarded as the dean of South African photography. When publishers asked where apartheid was in his pictures, he answered that it was embedded in their grain. Turning his lens on everyday architecture, he read in it the value systems of a society. He received the Hasselblad Award in 2006.
In this film, Goldblatt investigates how South African social and cultural influences shaped architecture, and what buildings reveal about the values of the society that built them.
